function.name: Music_3_LookupMusic
function.description: Retrieve a list of songs that align with the user's musical preferences based on artist, album, genre, and release year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist or band. Use 'dontcare' if this is not a filtering criterion.

album.description: The title of the album. Use 'dontcare' if this is not a filtering criterion.

genre.description: The musical genre of the songs. Select 'dontcare' to include all genres.

year.description: The release year of the song. Use 'dontcare' to include songs from any year.

message.reasoning: The user says: "Can you search for some rock music". They want to search for rock music. We have a function Music_3_LookupMusic that can retrieve a list of songs that align with user's musical preferences based on artist, album, genre, and release year. So we should call that function with genre set to "Rock". The other parameters can be default or unspecified. The user didn't specify artist, album, year. So we can set artist: "dontcare", album: "dontcare", genre: "Rock", year: "dontcare". The function signature expects year: number or "dontcare"? It says year?: number, default: "dontcare". So we can omit year or set to "dontcare"? The type says year?: number, default: "dontcare". That means if omitted, default is "dontcare". So we can just omit year. But we need to pass an object. We can pass {genre: "Rock"} and let defaults fill. But the function signature requires genre: "Reggae" | "Holiday" | ... | "dontcare". So we can pass genre: "Rock". The other fields optional. So we can call Music_3_LookupMusic with {genre: "Rock"}. That should return a list of songs. Then we can present them. The user didn't specify anything else. So we should call the function.
